title: Array, Structure and Map
goal: Choose an array, structure or map by the operations required for training requests.
prerequisites: onec.p2; P2: types, branching, loops and numeric boundaries.
outcomes: Choose an array, structure or map by the operations required for training requests.
Match three collection types to three operations.
sections: An array stores a sequence with zero-based indices, useful for traversing request lines. A structure describes a small record with known property names, such as Minutes and Rate. A map associates an admissible key with a value, such as a customer reference with an accumulated total. Choose by required operations rather than storing everything in one familiar type.

The service-desk calculation may be called from a card, document and report. Separate formulas let one fix leave two old implementations behind. A common computation contract avoids that divergence but needs explicit inputs. List every caller and verify equal units, parameter meaning and result type rather than merely matching function names.
Missing properties are a separate outcome

A structure’s Property method checks field existence and retrieves its value. Directly reading an absent property causes an error. Existence does not prove value validity: Minutes may be negative. Check existence, type and range in that order so a failure identifies the violated condition. Agree in advance what Undefined means as a map value.

Describe a function by inputs, preconditions, result and permitted changes. Cost uses numeric minutes/rate, admissible ranges, a rounded number and unchanged input collections. This description selects tests before implementation. If failure returns another type, callers must know explicitly or an error can accidentally participate in arithmetic. A stable contract makes substitution and review possible.

Two customers can share a name but have different references. Grouping by name silently combines their totals. Use references or an explicitly defined stable external code for customer calculations; keep names as presentation. Include equal names with different keys and repeated use of one key with a new value in the test.

Checking mutation needs more than comparing variable names:two variables can refer to one collection. Snapshot important fields and nested elements before execution, then compare the source afterwards. Run another function on the same input to expose hidden contamination. Keep each test’s setup independent so changing test order cannot alter the outcome.

Assigning a collection to another variable does not guarantee an independent copy of nested objects. Build a new array and explicitly create new structures if their contents will change. Verify source fields after computing the result. Avoid removing elements from the traversed source without a proven algorithm: select the desired elements into a new collection first.

A semantic negative control differs from a syntax error. Replacing addition with subtraction may compile but must change a named assertion’s result. Keep compilation and executed assertions as separate outcomes. Unavailable platforms, timeouts and incomplete case lists cannot confirm missing results. Preserve original and mutated source hashes and identify the particular assertion that detects the defect.
